question: Does parameterized mechanism deduplication reduce total end-to-end workflow cost per successful task compared to literal mechanism replay, when model selection, mechanism resolution, browser execution, and verification costs are all measured on a fixed task corpus?
hypothesis: The deduplicated parameterized registry (25 mechanisms) reduces total workflow cost versus the full literal registry (32 mechanisms) because: (1) fewer mechanisms to evaluate during selection reduces model selection tokens; (2) token savings from storing shared patterns once outweigh per-mechanism resolution overhead; (3) browser execution and verification costs are identical across conditions (same actions executed). Net workflow savings exceed the parent's 14.16% storage-level savings because selection cost scales with registry size.
falsifier: Total workflow cost for parameterized condition is higher than literal condition when all costs (selection + resolution + execution + verification) are summed, OR the parameterized condition achieves lower success rate due to binding/resolution failures, OR selection tokens for parameterized are higher than literal despite smaller registry.

baselines.description: Full literal registry (32 concrete-URL mechanisms). Model selects from all 32 mechanisms and executes the matched one directly.
baselines.expected_behavior: Model evaluates all 32 mechanisms during selection; selection token cost scales with registry size; no resolution step needed; execution and verification proceed on concrete URL.

baselines.description: Deduplicated parameterized registry (25 mechanisms with ${slot} templates). Model selects from 25 mechanisms and resolves the matched template to concrete URL.
baselines.expected_behavior: Model evaluates 25 mechanisms during selection (reduced from 32); resolution adds one model call to fill slot; execution and verification proceed on resolved URL.

baselines.description: No registry. Model must generate the correct URL from the task goal without any mechanism guidance.
baselines.expected_behavior: Model uses task goal only; no selection or resolution cost; but may have lower success rate or higher exploration cost. Included as lower-bound cost reference (may be cheapest or most expensive depending on model capability).

positive_control.description: The 5 blog-read-post tasks that share GET /posts/{id} pattern must resolve to 1 parameterized mechanism in the parameterized condition, and the model must select this single mechanism for all 5 tasks.
positive_control.expected_behavior: Parameterized selection for all 5 blog-read-post tasks selects the same mechanism key; resolution fills ${id_0} with the correct concrete ID; bound_action matches the literal URL.

null_control.description: Tasks with unique patterns (no sharing) should show parameterized selection cost <= literal selection cost (fewer mechanisms to evaluate) but higher per-task resolution cost (extra model call for slot filling). Net effect for unique patterns is expected to be approximately neutral or slightly negative (parameterized slightly more expensive per task).
null_control.expected_behavior: For unique-pattern tasks, parameterized total workflow cost is within 30% of literal total workflow cost (resolution overhead partially offset by smaller registry). If parameterized cost exceeds literal by >50% for unique patterns, the deduplication overhead is not justified even at corpus level.

measurement_validity: Both conditions must use identical task definitions, model, and temperature from the parent synthetic corpus (32 tasks across 6 domains)
Model selection tokens measured via tiktoken cl100k_base on the full prompt+response for mechanism selection step
Resolution tokens measured separately for parameterized condition only (model call to fill ${slot} in selected template)
Browser execution cost measured as count of Playwright page interactions (clicks, navigations, form fills, screenshots)
Verification cost measured as count of model calls for post-execution state verification
Success rate measured as fraction of tasks where final state matches expected outcome
Registry size (mechanism count) recorded for both conditions as an independent check on deduplication
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of: (C1) both conditions achieve 100% success rate on the task corpus; (C2) parameterized selection tokens <= literal selection tokens (fewer mechanisms = fewer or equal selection tokens); (C3) total workflow cost (selection + resolution + browser + verification) for parameterized <= total workflow cost for literal; (C4) positive control passes (shared patterns resolve correctly); (C5) null control passes (unique-pattern overhead <= 50%). FALSIFIED if any condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents completion of either condition.
product_consequence_positive: If parameterized workflow cost <= literal cost with equal success rate, the 14.16% storage-level savings from parent translates to end-to-end workflow savings. Proceed to C-PRODUCT-ECON validation with real SPIDER registry and broader task families.
product_consequence_negative: If parameterized workflow cost > literal cost or success rate drops, storage-level deduplication does not translate to workflow savings. Close token-based inheritance economics and redirect product lane to alternative mechanisms (registry compression, retrieval efficiency, or orthogonal product capabilities).
estimated_cost: Low-medium — requires model API calls for selection/resolution/verification across 32 tasks x 2 conditions x 3 baselines = ~192 model invocations. Estimated <50K total tokens. No browser execution needed for the discriminating measurement (selection+resolution cost only); browser execution can be omitted if selection+resolution cost difference is already decisive.
expected_information_gain: High — directly answers the parent's unresolved question 'whether retrieval/verification/repair costs with fewer mechanisms actually reduce end-to-end amortized cost.' Changes product lane direction if negative (close token-based economics) or positive (proceed to real-corpus validation). The smallest experiment that can change the C-PRODUCT-ECON claim from HYPOTHESIS to either REJECTED or VALIDATED.
